title: Customer signal tiling and mini-asks inventory (rough)
content:
Summary:
A compact roll-up of recent customer threads (Nov 2029 — Dec 2029) focused on inference economics, observability gaps, and small UX fixes that unblock adoption for platform and product teams. This is intentionally a lightweight ‘tiling’ exercise: group repeating asks, surface low-effort high-impact fixes, and capture hypotheses we can validate in a 1–2 sprint probe.

Topline themes (what customers keep saying):
- Cost transparency gaps: customers want token-level cost explanations tied to routes/models and insight why a particular call cost more than an earlier sample. (Mostly Hosted API + Dedicated)
- Latency jitter and regional fallbacks: intermittent spikes in p95 when fallback to variant models triggers — customers surface that rollout policies are opaque.
- Embeddings quality vs. cost tradeoffs: requests for automated guidance (e.g., recommend vector size / model variant based on retrieval workload).
- Dev DX: SDK error messages are sometimes unhelpful for auth/VPC failures; engineers prefer a short triage checklist in the error payload.
- Small UX asks: per-route throttling UI, clearer quota exhaustion messages, and ability to label model variants in console for easy canaries.

Representative customer notes (verbatim snippets from threads):
- "We saw 2.4x cost on the same endpoint after the model swap — need the breakdown or we will pin older model."
- "When our VPC link fails we get a generic 502. Took our infra lead 40 minutes to find the misconfigured SG rule."
- "Embedding mismatch: recall dropped after quantization change. Is there an auto-scan that warns about quality risk?"

Prioritized micro-asks (1–3 day dev effort where possible):
1) Per-request cost snapshot API field: add cost_breakdown_hint (small JSON string) returned in response metadata indicating tokens, model, and an estimated micro-cost bucket (low/med/high). Impact: immediate reduction in billing tickets and easier triage. Owner: Customer Success + Runtime PM.

2) Console toggle: label model_variant with free-text tag (e.g., "canary-1") + show last-deploy-id. Low UI effort; helps customers map routes to canaries. Owner: Console UX.

3) SDK auth error enrichment: common auth errors map to suggested fixes (link to VPC checklist). Add short troubleshooting steps to error message. Impact: cuts ops time on support calls. Owner: Developer Experience.

4) Quick telemetry probe: add a p95-by-model-variant time-series (7d window) to rollout dashboard so customers can immediately spot variant regression. Owner: Observability.

Medium-effort proposals (2–6 sprints):
- Request-level cost attribution in Console / API: persistent per-route dashboards showing token distribution, per-caller costs, and a regression alert when cost per token changes > 20%.
- Embedding quality audit runner: automated comparison harness that re-embeds a sampled prompt set in candidate quantized model and reports recall drift (thresholded). Integrate as a pre-rollout guard.
- Smart fallback transparency: when smart routing falls back to compatible variant, emit an annotated audit event (model_from, model_to, reason) available in console trace viewer and as an optional webhook.

Low-effort mitigations we can ship now (internal):
- Triage doc for CS engineers: quick steps for common VPC/auth/502 issues (copy to Slack snippet).
- Rapid-runbook: how to pin model versions and force no-fallback for critical endpoints.

Validation plan (how we know these help):
- Roll out cost_breakdown_hint to 10 pilot customers, measure drop in billing-related tickets and mean time to resolution (target 30% reduction).
- A/B rollout label tags to new Console users and track frequency of accidental model swaps and canary confusion.
- Add SDK enrichment to dev builds and measure support contact volume for auth/VPC faults.

Risks and open questions:
- Cost exposure vs. leakage: exposing too much micro-cost data could be confusing; need guardrails and language that emphasizes estimates not exact billing.
- Telemetry volume: p95-by-variant increases metrics cardinality — cost/infra tradeoff to evaluate.
- Legal/contract: reserved capacity customers may have different needs for fallback notification vs. shared hosts; check SLA language.

Customer quotes for CS pitches (short pithy lines):
- "A single line that explains why a request cost more would have saved hours."
- "Labeling variants in the console would have prevented our canary from becoming prod."

Action items (owners + dates):
- Aisha: draft cost_breakdown_hint field spec and example payload (due 2029-12-10).
- Liam Park: prototype console model-variant-label UI (mock + acceptance criteria) (due 2029-12-12).
- Maya Chen: assemble pilot customer list and outreach email template for cost snapshot pilot (due 2029-12-09).
- Diego Alvarez: quick telemetry feasibility note on p95-by-variant card (due 2029-12-11).

Slack / tickets referenced:
- #cs-billing-thread (Dec 2029) — many of these quotes pulled from that thread.
- JIRA-CS-881 — customer report: "unexpected cost jump after model switch".

Notes to self / rough thinking (messy):
- Could we reuse Optimize heuristics for embeddings recommendations? Probably — ping Optimize PM for reuse.
- Might be able to prototype cost_breakdown_hint as a sampling feature first (not all requests) to reduce privacy/billing exposure.
- UX wording is critical: call it "cost snapshot" not "price tag" to reduce alarm.

Appendix: quick data signals to pull for validation (queries to run)
- Count of billing tickets referencing "model swap" or "cost spike" in last 90d.
- Distribution of p95 latency by region for top 10 customers.
- Number of support cases where error message is "502" and root cause ends up being VPC/NAT/SG.

End.
